title: Subjective Isms? On the Danger of Conflating Hate and Offence in Abusive Language Detection
reasoning: The paper is a position paper focusing on the theoretical definitions of 'isms' (hate speech) versus offence in NLP annotation. While it utilizes philosophical concepts such as subjectivity and standpoint theory, and defines offence through moral outrage, it does not evaluate or benchmark religion, faith systems, or specific moral/ethical codes. The inclusion of a standard 'Ethical Considerations' section does not qualify it for this category.
